title: Network Policy Agent v1.3.5+ assumes the ClusterPolicyEndpoint CRD and aws-node RBAC for it

detection.reason: the rule asks whether a CRD and an RBAC grant are ABSENT; the hint names the networking.k8s.aws CRDs that are present

quote: Removing CPE CRD checks as the CRD should be installed by default
remediation: From Network Policy Agent v1.3.5 (bundled with CNI v1.21.2) the agent watches clusterpolicyendpoints.networking.k8s.aws without first checking the CRD exists, and v1.21.0/v1.21.1 add aws-node ClusterRole rules for clusterpolicyendpoints, clusterpolicyendpoints/status and the /apis/networking.k8s.aws discovery URL. On EKS the control plane's network policy controller installs the CRD; on a self-managed install it comes from the aws-network-policy-agent project, not the VPC CNI chart. Before enabling enforcement on an agent at v1.3.5+, make sure both the CRD and the release ClusterRole are present.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd clusterpolicyendpoints.networking.k8s.aws -o name 2>/dev/null || echo 'MISSING CRD clusterpolicyendpoints.networking.k8s.aws'; kubectl auth can-i list clusterpolicyendpoints.networking.k8s.aws --as=system:serviceaccount:kube-system:aws-node  # MISSING or 'no' = the v1.3.5+ agent cannot watch ClusterPolicyEndpoints once enforcement is on
